evidence: Every one of the 55 criteria (render 1, constraints 2, functional 43, polish 6, visual 3) names a browser-observable outcome; none relies on a source read, a 'looks right' binary judgment, or a response-shape assertion without a state change. Durable evidence is required where state matters: cw_shared_saved_record (gate) clears all origin storage and reloads twice; cw_save_reload_restart requires the restart_app tool and a fresh page re-read of title/filename/source/revision/history; cw_stale_save_refused, cw_history_restore_adds_revision and cw_restore_request_repeat_safe all end on a fresh-page/third-page read of the record ('a freshly loaded page must show exactly three revisions'); the replay's reply status is only noted, not graded. Negative claims carry positive controls (e.g. cw_stop_cancels_pending_work control marker, cw_dynamic_code_refused harmless-strings control, cw_preview_isolation save/health/localStorage controls, cw_format_error_keeps_draft valid control). Probes are distinctive and leave traces: payload markers built from joined halves so the whole marker never appears in source (cw_dynamic_code_refused), hostile marker checked against title/library/localStorage, unique titles for every saved record, required pixel/input survival for last-good. The constraints gate inspects the live DOM read-only (observable DOM facts, not implementation files). Visual likert criteria follow the template's anchored-likert craft pattern and are not binary 'looks right' checks. Actual-run evidence: the v10 Oracle reward-details shows the configured judge (claude-code/glm-5.3-flashx) produced concrete quoted observations for 42/43 functional and 6/6 polish criteria (e.g. cw_restore_request_repeat_safe: 'POST /api/snippets/6/restore [200] ... A freshly loaded page showed exactly [Revision 3 ..., Revision 2, Revision 1]'; cw_last_good_recovery: 'pixel (60,40) ... 255,0,170,255'). Counterexamples tried: localStorage-only save app fails the gate after storage clearing and cw_live_library_update across contexts; a no-op Stop fails because a control marker plus visible stop reason are required; a restore endpoint that echoes success but adds a revision fails on the fresh-page count; a canvas-drawn editor remains decidable (screenshots allowed); an app that leaves focus on Run after Run still passes cw_newer_run_supersedes because the criterion says 'click into the code'. Risk=true because the one criterion the actual judge could not decide on v10 (cw_newer_run_supersedes, reasoning: 'the editor does not accept the source replacement while the run is active ... the newer Run could not be started in time') was reworded for v11 to a single Playwright code-runner action, and no configured judge run exists on these bytes to show it is now decidable.
notes: cw_newer_run_supersedes (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:312-318): the v11 wording ('do the Run, the replacement and the second Run in one Playwright code-runner action ... click into the code, select all with the keyboard, type the new line') is plausibly decidable, but the scripted golden check (runtime.cjs:165-178) does not click into the code; it relies on the golden's new editor.focus() after Run ('Straight after Run the code area has focus'), so the judge's exact click-then-select-all sequence on the golden is unmeasured. The void-twice-then-fail clause can still attribute judge slowness to the submission; the feasibility half belongs to the tool-feasibility row, recorded here as residual risk.

Timing windows are lenient relative to the public note (live library 'within about five seconds' graded at ten seconds; time limit 'within about ten seconds'), which keeps them decidable without sub-second precision.
Visual likert criteria (cw_visual_*) are judgment-based by design and match the template's anchored likert format; not a row-32 defect.
